meta_description_en: Letters from readers in Outlet magazine: ZX Spectrum +2 compatibility, screen dumps, Interface 1 and networking, Opus Discovery support, and Tasword usage.
meta_description_ru: Письма читателей в редакцию журнала Outlet: особенности ZX Spectrum +2, дамп экрана, Interface 1 и сеть, поддержка Opus Discovery и работа с Tasword.
body_en_plain:
May, 1988            Page  Reply
 Harry Harper.........02    03

 Ian Jones............04    04

 Mark Juby............05    05

 Dennis Ashley........06    07

 David Gent...........08    15

 Mike Haine...........17    21

 John Nicholls........22    26

From: Harry Harper, Coventry

Dear Brian,

I am not too well versed in
computers and do not write my
own programs(BASIC or M/C)merely
alter the odd prog. to my own
needs. That is why I welcomed
your tip in Issue No.4 - how to
INPUT in lines 23, 24. There are
enough tips for the"smart alecs"
- please keep supplying the
simple minds. I missed OUTCLASS
in Issue No.7.

I have upgraded to a Spec+2.Will
you be featuring programs that
exploit its sound chip and extra
memory? E.g. database etc. Are
the adverts still free as I may

be using your columns to sell
off my old Spec+?
                  Best Regards,
                   Harry Harper

P.S. I have been looking for a
screen dump for my printer: the
CGP 115 but when you consider
how long it took to print this
note I am not sure that I can
afford it.Time taken:5min.20sec.
PPS.Is it possible to extend the
print facility to the Contents?

 OUTCLASS will be more regular
starting next month, Harry but
128K programs are unlikely due
to problems with 48K users (like
me!).As for dumps- try HURRYDUMP
in this issue(for text only) and
use the Editorial now to print
the Contents. - Brian

From: Ian Jones
  ...may I suggest that you have
some articles on other aspects
of Interface One such as the
network?

Do you know of any books on the
microdrive and Interface 1 as I
understand the m/drive handbook
by Dr. Ian Logan is out of print
            Regards, Ian Jones
"Master your ZX Microdrive" from
HiSoft,The Old School,Greenfield
Bedford MK45 5DE (`6.95 I think)
Try book shops for old stocks of
books- even your local library!

You really need TWO interfaces
to check out networking properly
and write about it authoritively
which rules me out! Anyone able
to send an article?     - Brian

From Mark Juby, West Sussex

Dear Brian & Ron,
..Don't take any notice of those
fuddy-duddies who want you to
exclude games from the magazine.
My kids love "The Ticket".

The programming tips and utilit-
ies are fantastic but please
have some more of specific use
to us Discovery Users...
                Yours sincerely,
                  Mark R. Juby
After the exhaustive development
and testing needed for "Ticket"
I really appreciate our readers'
enthusiasm! Now,we've one or two
Opus-specific items coming (Note
CHECKOUT 1 in this issue)and I'm
giving much thought to this area
of imbalance.          - Brian

From Dennis Ashley, Pinner

Dear Ron,
What is this Jotter program? I
am not versed in BASIC although
I have started reading "30 Hour
Basic".I like messing about with
the Spectrum and altering exist-
ing programs in a simple manner
but I have not had the need to
produce original programs. I do
like using my Tasword to write
letters and I want to experiment
with your print graphics in my
future correspondence, like the
elongated font you demonstrated
on Disc 005 but I have never
"poked" (I must be careful how I
phrase that!) so when the
instructions said do just that,I
was worried that I would not be
able to go back to normal print.

This letter is beginning to
sound like a letter to an "agony
aunt" so one last comment. Do I
have to become a BASIC programm-
er to integrate the various rou-
tines, or can the instructions
be a little more explicit?
            Regards,
              Dennis
JOTTER is a simple message pad
program in m/drive Issue 1 or
disc Issue 4 so everyone has the
means to send us a letter. Don't
worry about using POKE-you can't
harm your computer. If something
goes wrong just switch off and
on again! Many of our utilities
are of use to those with some
programming ability but a coming
series of OUTCLASSes will try to
make things clearer and give you
something to refer to.  -  Brian

            DAVID GENT,
             31, BROOKSIDE AVE',
              BRUNSWICK VILL',
               NCLE'-ON-TYNE,
                NE13  7DP,
                 8/4/88.

 Dear Ron & Brian,

        thanks for issue 8 of
your Outlet Magazine, glad to
see it is up to normal standard.

 Now for a few points you or
your subscribers may be be able
to help me with.

I don't know if you can remember
but i once asked for any info on
Teletext Adapters for the 128K
Spectrum, as i was looking to


buy one, if anybody has one or
knows of a make that would be
compatible with the 128, then
they are quite welcome to write
to me if you could publish my
address, hope somebody can help
me with this matter.

 Now for an idea that may be
possible to incorporate into
Outlet, how about running a
swapshop of software and books.
I can understand there would be
quite an amount of paperwork and
list keeping invloved with such
a venture, but perhaps it could
be feasible.

 And another problem, i have
issue 2 of Outlet with the
master JigBlox program on it,

now when i load a fresh
competition picture it works
fine from the keyboard, but if i
redefine the keys for my
Interface 2 it will work for a
short time, but long before the
picture is complete the Basic
prog' becomes corrupted, and i
lose the last part of the
program when it becomes garbage.

 As i said it will work fine
from the keyboard so there is no
panic, but i was just wondering
if you knew about this quirk.

 On the subject of JigBlox, i
would just like to state my
opinion on it, i would NOT like
to see it aborted completely, as
i really do enjoy it, (mind you

i may be biased, as i did win
the last one, and because of
which i am well chuffed.)

 Now for any 128K owners i have
found a couple of pokes which
will alter the renumber facility
on the main menu. On power up
the default is :-

   Start Line = 10
   Increase Step = 10

You can poke 23444/5 with the
new start line in the usual Z80
format of low byte first, [see
OUTCLASS ISSUE 10!] and then
poke 23446/7 in the same way
with the new step value.

 An interesting quirk you may

like to try is poke 23444,0 on
power up then select RENUMBER
from the EDIT menu.

 Now may i suggest another
magazine you could perhaps
include in your Look Out
feature, this being Micro
Computer Mart, although it is
basically a second hand buy&sell
mag, it does include news and
feature reports along with a
clubs page and a few other
features, it costs 50 pence and
comes out every fortnight.

 Another point you could perhaps
help me with, i have recently
seen spelling checkers for the
larger computers and was
wondering if there is any

available for the Spectrum.
 I understand the limitations of
the Spectrum, but perhaps with
the 128K machine and 2
Micro-Drives it could be
possible to obtain quite a
respectable size database of
words, as my spelling verges on
the atrocious this would be
ideal for me, perhaps patched
into Tasword.

 Now as a reward for getting
this far through my letter i
will shower some praise on you,
i have been most impressed by
the standard you have started
and hope you can maintain and
perhaps improve on this. But the
one thing which has really made
me a loyal supporter so quickly

is the intimate atmosphere which
surrounds your magazine, as an
example, the fact that you not
only replaced two cartridges
which refused to load you also
included the postage i had used.
 It is little things like this
that will set you apart from the
big companies of this industry,
and will give the readers the
feeling of being a part of
Outlet. I sincerely hope you can
keep this attitude as it most
refreshing.


         Yours sincerely


           David Gent

To: David Gent from Brian


I'm not sure what role you see
us playing in this swapshop idea
David. To begin with anyone can
send a swaps message to OUTBOARD
for hard or software (but this
MUST be ORIGINAL software).Let's
take it from there. Anyone else
have any ideas on this?

Now, JIG!BLOX!. I have had the
odd crash but couldn't re-create
it and put it down to mains
fluctuations. It's odd that the
program seems to work normally.
What keys do you use when you
re-define? I wonder if it's a
flag getting corrupted somewhere
by your Interface 2?

The problem with including Micro
Mart in OUTLOOK is the same as
for Popular Computing Weekly.
OUTLET is despatched over the
first week of the month but it's
completed, ready for final
testing and duplication a week
before that so a new MART could
well be out before many of our
readers had read about the last
one!

The only spelling checker for
the Spectrum as far as I know is
TAS-SPELL from  Tasman  Software
but this is for the +3 only.Tell
you what, I'll start you  off:-
You spell "i" er... with an "I"!
Actually, I've always wanted  to
write a spelling checker myself
a simple one might not be too
difficult...         - Brian

From: Mike Haine, Leamingto Spa

   Hi Ron & Brian.

  Echo all the praise!!!

     Re. the tape version idea;
Surely the thing is to wait for
the megabyte disc system? Think
what that will do!!!

  I would like to push the idea
of a questionaire. It could be
included in the envelopes. Would
you like me to prepare one?

 The Spectrum can be very
reliable, if a few precautions
are taken. I found the biggest
improvement occurred when I
fixed the various add-ons so


that they couldn't move about. I
did this with rubber bands,
sticky pads etc. Never had
trouble since. The best way to
extend the Spectrum would
probably be to buy another and
run 2 in tandem. (Very interest-
ing project)!

 Do urge subscribers to quote
Prestel numbers. I agree that
too much emphasis on Prestel
would be a bad thing. However it
would be nice to use it to chat
to others and, used carefully,
could greatly enhance the mag.
 Also it could advertise Prestel
and Micronet (try them???) Frank
Harrop; are you on Prestel? (I
am 74 and would like to
contact!)

 On subject of printing; my
routine to print Outlook in four
columns is almost working. Sorry
about delay, have been diverted
to a routine to send progs by
hex codes on Prestel mbxs. Re.
Your query Ron. I see no reason
why it shouldn't be a once for
all prog. The routine I use to
print 16 Prestel frames on an A4
sheet on my RX80 printer. is
less than 200 bytes and 2 lines
of BASIC to call it. I really
will push on with it now.
(Trouble with being an AB
(Ancient Briton) is that one
goes awful slow. Re.M.Battison's
remark; it should be easy to
adapt the routine to any 8 pin
dot matrix printer; (other pin
numbers, a bit more difficult).

A dot addressable graphics
facility is required, though if
the printing were limited to
text only (no graphics), this is
not necessary.

 My thanks to Frank for his
support to my hex arguments.

 I agree Tasword 3 is an
improvement on Tasword 2.
However the latter is much
easier to modify to suit
particular requirements. I hope
to describe some such shortly.

 I like Tom's idea on
housekeeping. I would be
interesting to collect ideas and
put then together in an
integrated housekeeping system.

 I have my own system which
includes a card index with a
full CAT (including header
details), of each cart and tape
on separate cards. I have
started a prog to collect all
the Cats on one cart and then
sort them in alpha/bet. order
and print a full list with cart
numbers etc. (Will possibly get
finished sometime!).

      Mike Haine.(788832249)

We must postpone this idea of a
questionnaire for the time being
but we'll give it some more
thought later on. It will be
interesting to see how your
printing ideas work out though.

                     - Brian

From: John Nicholls, BIRMINGHAM

Dear Ron & Brian,

 I have already written to thank
you for OUTLET Issue No 007, but
at the time of writing I had
read little more than SHOUTBURST
and you got me started on one of
my pet hobby-horses(i.e. putting
the world to rights).

 I have now spent no little time
with the rest of the issue, and
am once again delighted at the
quality of the contents.

 HANDYWIDE is indeed the very
utility which I desired, though
I had given up all hope of ever
finding anything of this sort
after you so patiently explained

why such a utility would be
impossible to write. Then you
went ahead and did it!!

 Truly, I would have been pre-
pared to pay quite a few pounds
for such a program, and it is
very good of you to give such
programs away with OUTLET. I
forget how much I paid for
Tasman's TASWIDE,but it certain-
ly is not a patch on HANDYWIDE.

 Having received so much from
you since the launch of OUTLET,
I hesitate to ask for even more.
But not for long.

 Having performed the impossible
I have little doubt that some-
thing merely difficult will also
be feasible.

 I admire your print routines,
that is the "Set Up Printer",
"Print This Page"and "Print All"
options. I also liked the full
width printing obtained when
printing the Summary of Instruc-
tions in HANDYWIDE.

 Would it be possible to separ-
ate these routines and give them
to us in such a way that they
can be merged with our own - or
other - programs?

 For example, would it be
possible to merge these routines
into HANDYWIDE, and thus print
out the full instructions?

 Next, when printing a page, the
copy is normally only 32 chrs

wide, leaving half the width of
the paper unused. Is it possible
for you to include an option
which does the printing on the
right hand side of the page?
This would allow use to be made
of that side without removing
the paper and turning it upside
down.

 That's all for now!! Keep up
the good work. Especially
SHOUTBURST. It's nice to be able
to let off steam now and again,
even if no-one listens. Well, do
they ever?

   All the best to both of you,

           John.

To John Nicholls from Brian

I've not seen TASWIDE but it's
very gratifying to hear it's not
a patch on HANDYWIDE. I see that
TASWIDE is `5.50 with only 64
column printing and `9.95 for
the +3 version!(If only we could
afford a double-page spread in
Sinclair User etc. we could
charge `9.95 for OUTLET!)

Now, the print routines in our
"text mode" are not suitable for
merging into other programs to
print text but I've asked Ron to
try to put a dump of the full
HANDYWIDE instructions in your
envelope when he sends this
issue. As for the future, I'm
paying more attention to try to


give full dumps of instructions
- not easy for various reasons.
As for using the full width of
paper I'm waiting to see what
Mike Haine comes up with.Perhaps
we'll be able to do multi-column
dumps of text but there are many
difficulties - particularly of
compatibility with all systems.
                       - Brian.

От: Harry Harper, Coventry

Дорогой Brian,

Я не слишком хорошо разбираюсь в
компьютерах и не пишу собственных
программ (на Бейсике или в М/К),
а лишь подгоняю отдельные проги
под свои нужды. Поэтому я был
очень рад вашему совету в №4 —
как делать INPUT в строках 23 и
24. Хватит уже советов для
«умников» — пожалуйста, не
забывайте и о простых смертных.
Мне не хватало OUTCLASS в
выпуске №7.

Я обновился до Spec+2. Будут ли
у вас программы, использующие
его звуковой чип и память?
Например, база данных и т.д.
Объявления всё ещё бесплатны? Я,
возможно, воспользуюсь вашей

рубрикой, чтобы продать свой
старый Spec+?
             С наилучшими
               пожеланиями,
               Harry Harper

P.S. Я искал дамп экрана для
своего принтера CGP 115, но,
учитывая, сколько времени ушло
на печать этой записки, вряд ли
я могу себе это позволить. Время
печати: 5 мин. 20 сек.
PPS. Можно ли добавить печать
оглавления (Contents)?

 OUTCLASS станет регулярнее со
следующего месяца, Harry, но 128K
программы маловероятны из-за
проблем у пользователей 48K
(вроде меня!). Что до дампов —
попробуйте HURRYDUMP в этом номере
(только текст), а оглавление
теперь можно распечатать прямо из
Editorial. - Brian

От: Ian Jones
  ...могу ли я предложить вам
сделать несколько статей о других
возможностях Interface One,
например, о сети?

Не знаете ли вы каких-нибудь
книг по microdrive и Interface 1,
так как руководство по м/драйву
от Dr. Ian Logan, насколько я
знаю, уже не издается?
             С уважением,
               Ian Jones
"Master your ZX Microdrive" от
HiSoft, The Old School,
Greenfield, Bedford MK45 5DE
(кажется, £6.95). Проверьте
книжные магазины на остатки
старых тиражей — или местную
библиотеку!

Чтобы как следует протестировать
сеть и авторитетно о ней писать,
нужно ДВА интерфейса, а у меня
их нет! Может ли кто-нибудь
прислать статью?        - Brian

От: Mark Juby, West Sussex

Дорогие Brian и Ron,
..Не обращайте внимания на тех
старомодных брюзг, которые
требуют убрать игры из журнала.
Мои дети обожают "The Ticket".

Советы по программированию и
утилиты просто фантастические, но
добавьте, пожалуйста, больше
того, что пригодится именно нам,
пользователям Discovery...
             Искренне ваш,
               Mark R. Juby
После изнурительной разработки и
тестирования "Ticket" мне очень
приятен энтузиазм читателей! У
нас готовится пара вещей
специально под Opus (обратите
внимание на CHECKOUT 1 в этом
номере), и я всерьез думаю над
устранением этого дисбаланса.
                        - Brian

От: Dennis Ashley, Pinner

Дорогой Ron,
Что это за программа Jotter? Я
не силен в Бейсике, хотя начал
читать "30 Hour Basic". Мне
нравится возиться со Спектрумом
и слегка переделывать чужие
программы, но нужды писать что-то
с нуля пока не возникало. Зато
я люблю печатать письма в Tasword
и хочу поэкспериментировать с
вашей печатной графикой, вроде
того вытянутого шрифта с диска
005, но я никогда ничего не
«покал» (надо аккуратнее
выбирать выражения!), так что
когда в инструкции было велено
сделать именно это, я испугался,
что не смогу вернуть обычный
шрифт.

Письмо начинает походить на крик
души в колонку психологической
помощи, так что последний вопрос:
обязательно ли становиться
программистом на Бейсике, чтобы
встраивать разные процедуры, или
инструкции могут быть чуть более
подробными?
             С уважением,
               Dennis
JOTTER — простая программа-
блокнот в м/драйв-выпуске 1 или
дисковом выпуске 4, чтобы у всех
была возможность черкнуть нам
пару строк. Не бойтесь POKE —
компьютер вы этим не сломаете.
Если что-то пойдет не так, просто
выключите и включите его снова!
Многие утилиты рассчитаны на тех,
у кого есть хоть какой-то опыт,
но в грядущих выпусках OUTCLASS
мы постараемся всё разжевать и
дать вам надежное руководство.
                        - Brian

            DAVID GENT,
             31, BROOKSIDE AVE',
              BRUNSWICK VILL',
               NCLE'-ON-TYNE,
                NE13  7DP,
                 8/4/88.

 Дорогие Ron и Brian,

        спасибо за 8-й номер
вашего журнала Outlet, приятно
видеть, что планка по-прежнему
держится на высоте.

 А теперь пара вопросов, в
которых вы или подписчики могли
бы мне помочь.

Не знаю, помните ли вы, но я как-
то спрашивал про телетекст-
адаптеры для 128K Spectrum, так
как присматривал себе такой; если
у кого-то есть или кто-то знает

модель, совместимую со 128, пусть
напишут мне, если вы опубликуете
мой адрес. Надеюсь, кто-нибудь
откликнется.

 Еще идея, которую, возможно,
удастся воплотить в Outlet: как
насчет организации обменника
(swapshop) софтом и книгами?
Понимаю, что с этим связано много
бумажной волокиты и списков, но,
может, это осуществимо?

 И еще проблема: у меня есть
выпуск 2 Outlet с основной
программой JigBlox,

и когда я загружаю новую
картинку для конкурса, с
клавиатуры всё работает отлично,
но если переопределить клавиши
под мой Interface 2, игра
работает совсем недолго — задолго
до сборки картинки бейсик-прога
портится, и хвост программы
превращается в мусор.

 Как я уже сказал, с клавиатуры
всё работает нормально, паники
нет, но мне просто интересно,
знали ли вы об этом глюке.

 Что касается JigBlox, хотелось
бы высказать свое мнение: я бы
НЕ хотел, чтобы ее закрыли
совсем, она мне очень нравится
(хотя я могу быть предвзятым,

ведь в прошлый раз я победил и
был безумно этому рад).

 Для владельцев 128K я нашел
пару поков, меняющих функцию
перенумерации (renumber) в
главном меню. При включении по
умолчанию стоит:

   Start Line = 10
   Increase Step = 10

Можно сделать poke 23444/5 с
новым номером начальной строки в
привычном формате Z80 (младший
байт вперед, [см. OUTCLASS В
ВЫПУСКЕ 10!]), а затем poke
23446/7 точно так же с новым шагом.

 Любопытный трюк, который вы

можете попробовать: poke 23444,0
при включении, а затем выбрать
RENUMBER в меню EDIT.

 Могу ли я предложить еще один
журнал для вашей рубрики
Look Out — Micro Computer Mart?
Хотя по сути это газета частных
объявлений о купле-продаже б/у
железа, там есть новости, отчеты,
страничка клубов и другие
материалы; стоит 50 пенсов и
выходит раз в две недели.

 И еще кое-что, в чем вы, может,
поможете: я недавно видел
программы проверки орфографии для
больших компьютеров и подумал,
есть ли такие

для Спектрума.
 Я понимаю ограничения Спектрума,
но, возможно, на 128K машине и с
двумя Microdrive получилось бы
собрать базу слов приличного
размера. Поскольку моя грамотность
граничит с ужасом, для меня это
было бы идеальным решением — скажем,
в виде патча к Tasword.

 В награду за то, что дочитали
письмо до этого места, осыплю
вас похвалами: я был глубоко
поражен заданным вами уровнем и
надеюсь, что вы удержите и даже
поднимете планку. Но что сделало
меня вашим преданным читателем

так быстро — это душевная, почти
домашняя атмосфера журнала.
Пример тому: вы не только заменили
мне два картриджа, которые не
хотели грузиться, но и возместили
почтовые расходы.
 Именно такие мелочи отличают вас
от акул этой индустрии и дают
читателям ощущение причастности
к Outlet. Искренне надеюсь, что
вы сохраните такой подход, это
очень подкупает.

             Искренне ваш,

               David Gent

Для: David Gent от Brian

Не совсем понимаю, какую роль ты
отводишь нам в этом «обменнике»,
David. Для начала любой желающий
может отправить объявление об
обмене в OUTBOARD — будь то софт
или железо (но программы ДОЛЖНЫ
быть ОРИГИНАЛЬНЫМИ). Начнем с
этого. У кого-нибудь еще есть
мысли на этот счет?

Теперь насчет JIG!BLOX!. У меня
пару раз случались вылеты, но я
не смог их повторить и списал на
скачки напряжения. Странно, что
программа вроде бы работает штатно.
Какие клавиши ты выбираешь при
переопределении? Не портит ли твой
Interface 2 какой-нибудь флаг в
памяти?

С включением Micro Mart в OUTLOOK
та же беда, что и с Popular
Computing Weekly. OUTLET рассылается
в течение первой недели месяца, но
сдается на финальное тестирование и
тиражирование за неделю до этого,
так что свежий MART успеет выйти
до того, как наши читатели прочтут
про предыдущий!

Единственный спеллчекер для
Спектрума, о котором я знаю —
TAS-SPELL от Tasman Software, но
он только для +3. Знаешь что,
давай я дам тебе первый урок:
слово "i" (я)... пишется с
большой буквы "I"! А если серьезно,
я и сам всегда хотел написать
проверку орфографии — простенькую
сделать, пожалуй, не так уж и
трудно...               - Brian

От: Mike Haine, Leamington Spa

   Привет, Ron и Brian.

  Присоединяюсь ко всем похвалам!

     По поводу кассетной версии:
не разумнее ли дождаться дисковой
системы на мегабайт? Подумайте,
какие будут возможности!

  Хочу продвинуть идею анкеты-
опросника. Ее можно вкладывать
в конверты. Хотите, я составлю?

 Спектрум может быть весьма
надежным, если принять меры.
Главное улучшение у меня наступило,
когда я зафиксировал все разъемы
и интерфейсы,

чтобы они не болтались. Я сделал
это резинками, липучками и т.д.
С тех пор проблем не знаю. Лучший
способ расширить возможности
Спектрума — купить второй и
запустить их в тандеме. (Очень
любопытный проект)!

 Обязательно призовите читателей
делиться номерами Prestel. Согласен,
перегибать с Prestel не стоит.
Однако было бы здорово общаться
там друг с другом, и при грамотном
подходе это пошло бы журналу на
пользу.
 К тому же это реклама Prestel и
Micronet (попробуете???). Frank
Harrop, вы есть в Prestel? (Мне
74 года, очень хотелось бы
пообщаться!)
По поводу печати: моя процедура
для печати Outlook в четыре
колонки почти готова. Простите
за задержку, отвлекся на подпрог-
рамму передачи прог hex-кодами
через Prestel mbxs. Касательно
твоего вопроса, Ron. Я не вижу
причин, почему бы ей не стать
универсальной. Программа, кото-
рую я использую для печати 16
кадров Prestel на листе A4 на
моем принтере RX80, занимает
меньше 200 байт и 2 строки
BASIC для вызова. Теперь я
действительно налягу на нее.
(Беда с тем, чтобы быть AB
(Ancient Briton) — двигаешься
ужасно медленно. Насчет реплики
M.Battison: процедуру должно
быть легко адаптировать под любой
8-игольчатый матричный принтер;
(с другим числом иголок чуть
сложнее).

Требуется режим графики с адре-
сацией точек, хотя если печать
ограничена только текстом (без
графики), в этом нет нужды.

 Спасибо Frank за поддержку моих
доводов о hex.

 Согласен, Tasword 3 — шаг
вперед по сравнению с Tasword 2.
Однако последнюю гораздо проще
модифицировать под конкретные
нужды. Надеюсь вскоре описать
кое-что из этого.

 Мне нравится идея Tom насчет
каталогизации (housekeeping).
Было бы интересно собрать идеи
и свести их в единую систему
каталогизации.

 У меня есть своя система, вклю-
чающая картотеку с полным CAT
(включая данные заголовков) для
каждого cart и ленты на отдель-
ных карточках. Я начал прогу,
чтобы собрать все CAT на одном
cart, затем отсортировать их в
алфавитном порядке и напечатать
полный список с номерами cart
и т.д. (Возможно, когда-нибудь
доделаю!).

      Mike Haine.(788832249)

Нам пока придется отложить идею
с опросником, но мы вернемся
к ней позже. Впрочем, будет
интересно посмотреть, что выйдет
из твоих идей с печатью.

                     - Brian

От: John Nicholls, BIRMINGHAM

Дорогие Ron & Brian,

 Я уже писал, благодаря вас за
OUTLET Issue No 007, но на момент
написания я успел прочесть разве
что SHOUTBURST, и вы задели
одного из моих любимых коньков
(а именно: наведение порядка
в мире).

 Теперь я провел немало времени
за остальной частью номера и
снова в восторге от качества
материалов.

 HANDYWIDE — действительно та
самая утилита, о которой я меч-
тал, хотя я уже оставил всякую
надежду найти что-то подобное
после того, как вы так терпеливо

объяснили, почему написать такую
утилиту невозможно. А потом
взяли и сделали ее!!

 Воистину, я был бы готов выло-
жить немало фунтов за такую
программу, и очень мило с вашей
стороны раздавать подобные вещи
вместе с OUTLET. Не помню, сколь-
ко я отдал за Tasman's TASWIDE,
но она совершенно не идет ни в
какое сравнение с HANDYWIDE.

 Получив от вас так много с мо-
мента запуска OUTLET, я стесня-
юсь просить о еще большем.
Но ненадолго.

 Раз уж вы совершили невозмож-
ное, я почти не сомневаюсь, что
просто трудная задача вам тоже
будет по плечу.

 Я восхищен вашими процедурами
печати, то есть опциями "Set Up
Printer", "Print This Page" и
"Print All". Мне также понрави-
лась печать на всю ширину при
распечатке Summary of Instruc-
tions в HANDYWIDE.

 Можно ли выделить эти подпрог-
раммы и дать их нам так, чтобы
их можно было объединять с на-
шими — или чужими — программами?

 Например, можно ли внедрить эти
процедуры в HANDYWIDE и таким
образом распечатать полную ин-
струкцию?

 Далее, при печати страницы ко-
пия обычно занимает всего 32

символа в ширину, оставляя неис-
пользованной половину листа. Не
могли бы вы добавить опцию, ко-
торая печатает на правой поло-
вине страницы? Это позволило бы
использовать ту сторону, не из-
влекая бумагу и не переворачивая
ее вверх ногами.

 На этом пока все!! Продолжайте
в том же духе. Особенно
SHOUTBURST. Приятно иметь воз-
можность время от времени вы-
пустить пар, даже если никто не
слушает. Впрочем, слушают ли
вообще хоть когда-то?

   Всего наилучшего вам обоим,

           John.

Для John Nicholls от Brian

Я не видел TASWIDE, но очень ле-
стно слышать, что она и в под-
метки не годится HANDYWIDE.
Я смотрю, TASWIDE стоит `5.50
всего с 64-колоночной печатью
и `9.95 за версию для +3! (Если
бы мы только могли позволить себе
разворот в Sinclair User и т.д.,
мы могли бы брать `9.95 за
OUTLET!)

Что касается процедур печати в
нашем "text mode", они не подхо-
дят для внедрения в другие прог-
раммы для печати текста, но я
попросил Ron попробовать вложить
дамп полной инструкции к HANDYWIDE
в твой конверт, когда он будет
отправлять этот номер. На будущее
я уделяю больше внимания попыткам

выдавать полные дампы инструкций
— что непросто по ряду причин.
А насчет использования всей ши-
рины бумаги — жду, что придумает
Mike Haine. Возможно, мы сможем
делать многоколоночные дампы тек-
ста, но тут масса трудностей —
особенно совместимости со всеми
системами.
                       - Brian.

### From: Harry Harper, Coventry

Dear Brian,

I am not too well versed in computers and do not write my own programs (BASIC or M/C) merely alter the odd prog. to my own needs. That is why I welcomed your tip in Issue No.4 - how to INPUT in lines 23, 24. There are enough tips for the "smart alecs" - please keep supplying the simple minds. I missed OUTCLASS in Issue No.7.

I have upgraded to a Spec+2. Will you be featuring programs that exploit its sound chip and extra memory? E.g. database etc. Are the adverts still free as I may be using your columns to sell off my old Spec+?

Best Regards,  
Harry Harper

P.S. I have been looking for a screen dump for my printer: the CGP 115 but when you consider how long it took to print this note I am not sure that I can afford it. Time taken: 5min. 20sec.  
PPS. Is it possible to extend the print facility to the Contents?

> OUTCLASS will be more regular starting next month, Harry but 128K programs are unlikely due to problems with 48K users (like me!). As for dumps — try HURRYDUMP in this issue (for text only) and use the Editorial now to print the Contents.  
> — Brian

---

### From: Ian Jones

...may I suggest that you have some articles on other aspects of Interface One such as the network?

Do you know of any books on the microdrive and Interface 1 as I understand the m/drive handbook by Dr. Ian Logan is out of print.

Regards,  
Ian Jones

> "Master your ZX Microdrive" from HiSoft, The Old School, Greenfield Bedford MK45 5DE (£6.95 I think). Try book shops for old stocks of books — even your local library!
>
> You really need TWO interfaces to check out networking properly and write about it authoritively which rules me out! Anyone able to send an article?  
> — Brian

---

### From Mark Juby, West Sussex

Dear Brian & Ron,

..Don't take any notice of those fuddy-duddies who want you to exclude games from the magazine. My kids love "The Ticket".

The programming tips and utilities are fantastic but please have some more of specific use to us Discovery Users...

Yours sincerely,  
Mark R. Juby

> After the exhaustive development and testing needed for "Ticket" I really appreciate our readers' enthusiasm! Now, we've one or two Opus-specific items coming (Note CHECKOUT 1 in this issue) and I'm giving much thought to this area of imbalance.  
> — Brian

---

### From Dennis Ashley, Pinner

Dear Ron,

What is this Jotter program? I am not versed in BASIC although I have started reading "30 Hour Basic". I like messing about with the Spectrum and altering existing programs in a simple manner but I have not had the need to produce original programs. I do like using my Tasword to write letters and I want to experiment with your print graphics in my future correspondence, like the elongated font you demonstrated on Disc 005 but I have never "poked" (I must be careful how I phrase that!) so when the instructions said do just that, I was worried that I would not be able to go back to normal print.

This letter is beginning to sound like a letter to an "agony aunt" so one last comment. Do I have to become a BASIC programmer to integrate the various routines, or can the instructions be a little more explicit?

Regards,  
Dennis

> JOTTER is a simple message pad program in m/drive Issue 1 or disc Issue 4 so everyone has the means to send us a letter. Don't worry about using POKE — you can't harm your computer. If something goes wrong just switch off and on again! Many of our utilities are of use to those with some programming ability but a coming series of OUTCLASSes will try to make things clearer and give you something to refer to.  
> — Brian

---

```text
            DAVID GENT,
             31, BROOKSIDE AVE',
              BRUNSWICK VILL',
               NCLE'-ON-TYNE,
                NE13  7DP,
                 8/4/88.
```

Dear Ron & Brian,

thanks for issue 8 of your Outlet Magazine, glad to see it is up to normal standard.

Now for a few points you or your subscribers may be be able to help me with.

I don't know if you can remember but i once asked for any info on Teletext Adapters for the 128K Spectrum, as i was looking to buy one, if anybody has one or knows of a make that would be compatible with the 128, then they are quite welcome to write to me if you could publish my address, hope somebody can help me with this matter.

Now for an idea that may be possible to incorporate into Outlet, how about running a swapshop of software and books. I can understand there would be quite an amount of paperwork and list keeping invloved with such a venture, but perhaps it could be feasible.

And another problem, i have issue 2 of Outlet with the master JigBlox program on it, now when i load a fresh competition picture it works fine from the keyboard, but if i redefine the keys for my Interface 2 it will work for a short time, but long before the picture is complete the Basic prog' becomes corrupted, and i lose the last part of the program when it becomes garbage.

As i said it will work fine from the keyboard so there is no panic, but i was just wondering if you knew about this quirk.

On the subject of JigBlox, i would just like to state my opinion on it, i would NOT like to see it aborted completely, as i really do enjoy it, (mind you i may be biased, as i did win the last one, and because of which i am well chuffed.)

Now for any 128K owners i have found a couple of pokes which will alter the renumber facility on the main menu. On power up the default is :-

```text
   Start Line = 10
   Increase Step = 10
```

You can poke 23444/5 with the new start line in the usual Z80 format of low byte first, [see OUTCLASS ISSUE 10!] and then poke 23446/7 in the same way with the new step value.

An interesting quirk you may like to try is poke 23444,0 on power up then select RENUMBER from the EDIT menu.

Now may i suggest another magazine you could perhaps include in your Look Out feature, this being Micro Computer Mart, although it is basically a second hand buy&sell mag, it does include news and feature reports along with a clubs page and a few other features, it costs 50 pence and comes out every fortnight.

Another point you could perhaps help me with, i have recently seen spelling checkers for the larger computers and was wondering if there is any available for the Spectrum.

I understand the limitations of the Spectrum, but perhaps with the 128K machine and 2 Micro-Drives it could be possible to obtain quite a respectable size database of words, as my spelling verges on the atrocious this would be ideal for me, perhaps patched into Tasword.

Now as a reward for getting this far through my letter i will shower some praise on you, i have been most impressed by the standard you have started and hope you can maintain and perhaps improve on this. But the one thing which has really made me a loyal supporter so quickly is the intimate atmosphere which surrounds your magazine, as an example, the fact that you not only replaced two cartridges which refused to load you also included the postage i had used.

It is little things like this that will set you apart from the big companies of this industry, and will give the readers the feeling of being a part of Outlet. I sincerely hope you can keep this attitude as it most refreshing.

Yours sincerely,  
David Gent

> **To: David Gent from Brian**
>
> I'm not sure what role you see us playing in this swapshop idea David. To begin with anyone can send a swaps message to OUTBOARD for hard or software (but this MUST be ORIGINAL software). Let's take it from there. Anyone else have any ideas on this?
>
> Now, JIG!BLOX!. I have had the odd crash but couldn't re-create it and put it down to mains fluctuations. It's odd that the program seems to work normally. What keys do you use when you re-define? I wonder if it's a flag getting corrupted somewhere by your Interface 2?
>
> The problem with including Micro Mart in OUTLOOK is the same as for Popular Computing Weekly. OUTLET is despatched over the first week of the month but it's completed, ready for final testing and duplication a week before that so a new MART could well be out before many of our readers had read about the last one!
>
> The only spelling checker for the Spectrum as far as I know is TAS-SPELL from Tasman Software but this is for the +3 only. Tell you what, I'll start you off:— You spell "i" er... with an "I"! Actually, I've always wanted to write a spelling checker myself a simple one might not be too difficult...  
> — Brian

---

### From: Mike Haine, Leamington Spa

Hi Ron & Brian.

Echo all the praise!!!

Re. the tape version idea; Surely the thing is to wait for the megabyte disc system? Think what that will do!!!

I would like to push the idea of a questionnaire. It could be included in the envelopes. Would you like me to prepare one?

The Spectrum can be very reliable, if a few precautions are taken. I found the biggest improvement occurred when I fixed the various add-ons so that they couldn't move about. I did this with rubber bands, sticky pads etc. Never had trouble since. The best way to extend the Spectrum would probably be to buy another and run 2 in tandem. (Very interesting project)!

Do urge subscribers to quote Prestel numbers. I agree that too much emphasis on Prestel would be a bad thing. However it would be nice to use it to chat to others and, used carefully, could greatly enhance the mag. Also it could advertise Prestel and Micronet (try them???) Frank Harrop; are you on Prestel? (I am 74 and would like to contact!)

On subject of printing; my routine to print Outlook in four columns is almost working. Sorry about delay, have been diverted to a routine to send progs by hex codes on Prestel mbxs. Re. Your query Ron. I see no reason why it shouldn't be a once for all prog. The routine I use to print 16 Prestel frames on an A4 sheet on my RX80 printer is less than 200 bytes and 2 lines of BASIC to call it. I really will push on with it now. (Trouble with being an AB (Ancient Briton) is that one goes awful slow. Re. M.Battison's remark; it should be easy to adapt the routine to any 8 pin dot matrix printer; (other pin numbers, a bit more difficult).

A dot addressable graphics facility is required, though if the printing were limited to text only (no graphics), this is not necessary.

My thanks to Frank for his support to my hex arguments.

I agree Tasword 3 is an improvement on Tasword 2. However the latter is much easier to modify to suit particular requirements. I hope to describe some such shortly.

I like Tom's idea on housekeeping. I would be interesting to collect ideas and put then together in an integrated housekeeping system.

I have my own system which includes a card index with a full CAT (including header details), of each cart and tape on separate cards. I have started a prog to collect all the Cats on one cart and then sort them in alpha/bet. order and print a full list with cart numbers etc. (Will possibly get finished sometime!).

Mike Haine (788832249)

***

We must postpone this idea of a questionnaire for the time being but we'll give it some more thought later on. It will be interesting to see how your printing ideas work out though.

— Brian

---

### From: John Nicholls, BIRMINGHAM

Dear Ron & Brian,

I have already written to thank you for OUTLET Issue No 007, but at the time of writing I had read little more than SHOUTBURST and you got me started on one of my pet hobby-horses (i.e. putting the world to rights).

I have now spent no little time with the rest of the issue, and am once again delighted at the quality of the contents.

HANDYWIDE is indeed the very utility which I desired, though I had given up all hope of ever finding anything of this sort after you so patiently explained why such a utility would be impossible to write. Then you went ahead and did it!!

Truly, I would have been prepared to pay quite a few pounds for such a program, and it is very good of you to give such programs away with OUTLET. I forget how much I paid for Tasman's TASWIDE, but it certainly is not a patch on HANDYWIDE.

Having received so much from you since the launch of OUTLET, I hesitate to ask for even more. But not for long.

Having performed the impossible I have little doubt that something merely difficult will also be feasible.

I admire your print routines, that is the "Set Up Printer", "Print This Page" and "Print All" options. I also liked the full width printing obtained when printing the Summary of Instructions in HANDYWIDE.

Would it be possible to separate these routines and give them to us in such a way that they can be merged with our own — or other — programs?

For example, would it be possible to merge these routines into HANDYWIDE, and thus print out the full instructions?

Next, when printing a page, the copy is normally only 32 chrs wide, leaving half the width of the paper unused. Is it possible for you to include an option which does the printing on the right hand side of the page? This would allow use to be made of that side without removing the paper and turning it upside down.

That's all for now!! Keep up the good work. Especially SHOUTBURST. It's nice to be able to let off steam now and again, even if no-one listens. Well, do they ever?

All the best to both of you,

John.

***

### To John Nicholls from Brian

I've not seen TASWIDE but it's very gratifying to hear it's not a patch on HANDYWIDE. I see that TASWIDE is `5.50 with only 64 column printing and `9.95 for the +3 version! (If only we could afford a double-page spread in Sinclair User etc. we could charge `9.95 for OUTLET!)

Now, the print routines in our "text mode" are not suitable for merging into other programs to print text but I've asked Ron to try to put a dump of the full HANDYWIDE instructions in your envelope when he sends this issue. As for the future, I'm paying more attention to try to give full dumps of instructions — not easy for various reasons. As for using the full width of paper I'm waiting to see what Mike Haine comes up with. Perhaps we'll be able to do multi-column dumps of text but there are many difficulties — particularly of compatibility with all systems.

— Brian.

### От: Harry Harper, Coventry

Дорогой Brian,

Я не слишком хорошо разбираюсь в компьютерах и не пишу собственных программ (на Бейсике или в М/К), а лишь подгоняю отдельные проги под свои нужды. Поэтому я был очень рад вашему совету в №4 — как делать INPUT в строках 23 и 24. Хватит уже советов для «умников» — пожалуйста, не забывайте и о простых смертных.
